title: 📘 UNIT 3: NATURAL RESOURCE BASE OF ETHIOPIA
notes:
Natural resources → useful materials and features obtained from nature.

🌍 Major resources: Water • Soil • Minerals • Natural vegetation • Wildlife.

title: 📌 3.1 MEANING OF NATURAL RESOURCES
notes:
🌱 Renewable resources → resources that can be naturally replenished.

Examples: Plants • Animals • Soil • Water • Geothermal energy • Wind • Solar radiation.

⛏️ Non-renewable resources → limited resources that cannot be naturally regenerated within a short period.

Examples: Minerals • Coal • Crude oil • Natural gas.

title: ⚠️ PRESSURE ON NATURAL RESOURCES
notes:
Major pressures include:
• Population pressure
• Agricultural expansion
• Migration
• Urbanization
• Resettlement
• Climate change
• Environmental pollution

title: 📌 3.2 DRAINAGE SYSTEMS OF ETHIOPIA
notes:
Drainage system → the network of rivers and streams that drains an area.

🇪🇹 Ethiopia has 3 major drainage systems:
1️⃣ Western (Mediterranean Sea)
2️⃣ Southeastern (Indian Ocean)
3️⃣ Inland (Rift Valley)

title: 🌊 WESTERN DRAINAGE SYSTEM
notes:
➡️ Direction: Toward Sudan → Nile → Mediterranean Sea.

💧 Largest drainage system in Ethiopia; contributes about 60% of the country's annual water discharge.

Major rivers:
• Tekezze
• Abbay
• Baro-Akobo

title: 🌊 SOUTHEASTERN DRAINAGE SYSTEM
notes:
➡️ Direction: Toward the Indian Ocean through Somalia.

Major rivers:
• Wabe Shebelle
• Genale
• Dawa

📍 Drains much of southeastern Ethiopia.

title: 🏞️ INLAND (RIFT VALLEY) DRAINAGE SYSTEM
notes:
➡️ Rivers and streams drain into lakes and depressions within the Ethiopian Rift Valley.

🚫 Unlike the other systems, its waters do not reach the sea.

📍 Closely associated with the Rift Valley lakes.

title: 📌 3.3 WATER RESOURCES OF ETHIOPIA
notes:
💧 Ethiopia has abundant water resources mainly in the form of rivers and lakes.

🏔️ Most major rivers originate in the Ethiopian highlands and flow toward lowlands and neighboring countries.

title: 🏞️ MAJOR RIVERS OF ETHIOPIA
notes:
Important rivers:
• Tekezze
• Abbay
• Baro-Akobo
• Awash
• Wabe Shebelle
• Genale
• Dawa

⭐ Most originate in the highlands and flow toward lowlands or neighboring countries.

title: 💧 CHARACTERISTICS OF ETHIOPIAN RIVERS
notes:
• Mostly originate in highlands.
• Many have steep gradients and fast-flowing water.
• Many cross international boundaries.
• Flow varies seasonally with rainfall.
• Have high potential for irrigation and hydroelectric power.

title: 🏞️ LAKES OF ETHIOPIA
notes:
Major lake groups include:
🏔️ Highland lakes
🌋 Rift Valley lakes

⭐ Lake Tana → an important highland lake and source area of the Abbay River.

The Rift Valley contains a chain of lakes formed within the Rift Valley depression.

title: ⚡ SIGNIFICANCE OF RIVERS & LAKES
notes:
Water resources support:
⚡ Hydroelectric power
🌾 Irrigation
🎣 Fishing
🏠 Domestic water supply
🏭 Economic activities
🧳 Tourism and recreation

title: 📌 3.4 MAJOR SOIL TYPES OF ETHIOPIA
notes:
Soil → the upper layer of the Earth's surface that supports plant growth.

🇪🇹 Ethiopian soils are mainly derived from:
• Volcanic rocks
• Metamorphic rocks
• Sedimentary rocks

🌾 Soil is especially important because agriculture is a major economic activity.

title: 🌱 SOIL FORMATION
notes:
Soil formation is influenced by:
1️⃣ Parent material
2️⃣ Climate
3️⃣ Topography
4️⃣ Living organisms
5️⃣ Time

⛰️ Hill slopes → generally shallow soils due to erosion.

🌋 Volcanic plateaus with sufficient rainfall → commonly develop red and black basaltic soils.

title: 🌱 MAJOR SOIL TYPES OF ETHIOPIA
notes:
🇪🇹 Major soil types:
• Nitosols
• Vertisols
• Acrisols
• Cambisols
• Regosols
• Xerosols
• Yermosols
• Luvisols
• Fluvisols
• Lithosols

title: 🌾 IMPORTANT SOIL CHARACTERISTICS
notes:
🟤 Nitosols → volcanic soils; widely used for agriculture, including cereals, coffee and inset.

⚫ Vertisols → black, clay-rich soils; difficult to cultivate.

🏜️ Xerosols → shallow soils of arid/semi-arid areas; often saline and low in humus.

🏜️ Yermosols → desert/semi-desert soils; generally unsuitable for cultivation.

🟫 Luvisols → well-developed and nutrient-rich; among the better agricultural soils.

title: 🌱 OTHER SOIL CHARACTERISTICS
notes:
⛰️ Hard crystalline-rock areas → thin, rocky and generally poor soils.

🏜️ Afar → very shallow and saline soils associated with volcanic and dried-lake deposits.

🌾 Southeastern lowlands → sedimentary soils; low in nitrogen and humus but relatively rich in phosphorus and potash.

🌊 Alluvial soils → transported and deposited mainly along rivers; generally fertile.

title: 📌 3.5 MAJOR MINERAL RESOURCES
notes:
⛏️ Ethiopia has diverse mineral resources, although many deposits remain largely untapped.

Major groups:
🥇 Metallic minerals
🪨 Non-metallic minerals
🛢️ Energy minerals

title: 🥇 METALLIC MINERALS
notes:
Important metallic minerals include:

🥇 Gold → occurs in volcanic veins in Precambrian rocks and alluvial deposits; important occurrences include Adola, Bule Hora, Arero, Moyale, Akobo, Lega Dembi, Sakaro and Tigray.

⚪ Platinum → important deposits occur in western Ethiopia, including Yubdo, Gimbi and Akobo areas.

🔩 Tantalum → important deposit at Kenticha, southeast of Shakiso.

title: 🪨 NON-METALLIC MINERALS
notes:
Important non-metallic minerals include:

• Potash
• Common salt
• Soda ash
• Limestone

📌 Non-metallic minerals are produced in relatively greater amounts than metallic minerals.

title: 🛢️ ENERGY MINERAL RESOURCES
notes:
🛢️ Crude oil & natural gas → associated mainly with the Ogaden Basin.

⛏️ Coal → lignite deposits occur in parts of Shewa, Sidama and Wollega.

title: 💰 IMPORTANCE OF MINERAL RESOURCES
notes:
Mineral resources contribute to:
• Economic development
• Industrial development
• Employment
• Trade
• Export earnings

title: 📌 3.6 BIOTIC RESOURCES OF ETHIOPIA
notes:
Biotic resources → living components of an ecosystem.

🌿 Producers → green plants
🦁 Consumers → animals
🦠 Decomposers → bacteria and fungi

title: 🌿 3.6.1 NATURAL VEGETATION
notes:
Natural vegetation → plant communities that grow naturally without direct human cultivation.

🌍 Distribution is mainly influenced by:
• Altitude
• Climate
• Soil
• Drainage

Major vegetation types:
1️⃣ Afroalpine & Sub-Afroalpine
2️⃣ Forests
3️⃣ Woodland Savanna
4️⃣ Semi-desert & Desert vegetation

title: 🏔️ AFROALPINE & SUB-AFROALPINE VEGETATION
notes:
🏔️ Afroalpine → vegetation of the highest mountain environments; adapted to very cold conditions.

🌿 Sub-Afroalpine → mainly woodland shrubs.

Important species:
• Gibra (Lobelia rhynchopetalum)
• Asta (Erica arborea)

title: 🌳 FORESTS
notes:
Ethiopian forests occur mainly between about 450–3300 m altitude and in areas receiving about 200–2200 mm annual rainfall.

Two broad groups:
🌲 Highland forests
🌿 Lowland forests

title: 🌲 HIGHLAND FORESTS
notes:
📍 Mainly occur between 1500–3300 m.

🌲 Kerkha (Arundinaria) → 2800–3000 m
🌲 Tid (Juniperus procera) → 2200–2800 m
🌲 Zigba (Podocarpus) → 1800–2200 m
🌲 Woira (Olea africana) & Kosso (Hagenia abyssinica) → 1500–1800 m

title: 🌿 LOWLAND FORESTS
notes:
📍 Mainly occur below 1500 m.

Also called gallery or riverine forests because they commonly occur along rivers where soil moisture is available.

🌳 Common trees: Sholla and Warka.

🌧️ Where annual rainfall exceeds about 500 mm → Baphia forest predominates.

title: 🌾 WOODLAND SAVANNA
notes:
Woodland savanna → vegetation characterized by a mixture of woody plants and grasses.

📍 It is one of the major natural vegetation types of Ethiopia and occurs mainly under suitable warm and relatively dry environmental conditions.

title: 🏜️ SEMI-DESERT & DESERT VEGETATION
notes:
📍 Mainly found in Ethiopia’s dry lowlands.

🌵 Low rainfall and harsh conditions favor xerophytic plants → plants adapted to dry environments.

title: 🦁 WILDLIFE RESOURCES
notes:
Wildlife → undomesticated animals living in their natural habitats.

📍 Distribution depends mainly on:
• Altitude
• Climate
• Vegetation
• Availability of suitable habitats

🦌 Wildlife includes game animals and endemic animals.

title: 🦊 ENDEMIC ANIMALS
notes:
Endemic animal → an animal naturally restricted to a particular geographic area.

🇪🇹 Important Ethiopian endemic animals include:
• Walia Ibex
• Semien Fox

⚠️ Some endemic wildlife is threatened with extinction.

title: 🛡️ WILDLIFE CONSERVATION
notes:
Wildlife conservation → protection and proper management of wildlife and their habitats.

🎯 Main purpose → prevent extinction, protect biodiversity and maintain natural ecosystems.
